sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Defensive rotation is keeping the market's surface stable as Real Estate and Healthcare claim "all-green" status, but fading momentum in Technology and low agreement in Healthcare signal underlying fragility.

Defensive and rate-sensitive sectors are showing notable short-term strength. Real Estate (momentum 0.63, rank 4) and Healthcare (momentum 0.62, rank 8) have emerged as the only two "all-green" sectors, showing positive performance across the week, month, quarter, half, and YTD. Healthcare led the weekly gains by climbing 2 spots, while Industrials (momentum 0.80) remains a sustained powerhouse, gaining 1 spot to secure rank 2. 

Conversely, Technology is showing signs of exhaustion, slipping 1 spot to rank 3 despite holding a high momentum score of 0.73. Broad market laggards continue to drag on performance, with Consumer Cyclical stuck at the bottom of the board (momentum 0.08, rank 11) and Communication Services slipping further to rank 10 (momentum 0.23).

## Strength
* **All-Green Breadth:** Only 2 of 11 groups are positive across all timeframes (week, month, quarter, half, and YTD): Real Estate (momentum 0.63) and Healthcare (momentum 0.62).
* **Sustained Leadership:** Industrials remains exceptionally strong as a top-3 sector across 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons, holding the highest overall momentum score of 0.80 (rank 2).

## Movers & Momentum
* **Top Gainers:** Healthcare jumped 2 spots to rank 8 (momentum 0.62), while Industrials (+1 spot, rank 2), Real Estate (+1 spot, rank 4), and Utilities (+1 spot, rank 6, momentum 0.53) also improved their standings.
* **Momentum Leaders:** Industrials (0.80), Technology (0.73), and Real Estate (0.63) lead the board, while Energy holds the YTD rank 1 spot with a momentum score of 0.53.
* **Momentum Laggards:** Consumer Cyclical remains anchored at the bottom with a weak momentum score of 0.08 (rank 11), followed by Communication Services at 0.23 (rank 10) and Consumer Defensive at 0.42 (rank 7).

## Divergences
* **Technology Fading:** Despite holding high momentum (0.73), Technology's rank slipped by 1 spot over the last 5 days to rank 3, signaling a potential early-warning fade.
* **Fragile Healthcare Strength:** Although Healthcare is "all-green" and gained 2 spots, it exhibits a low agreement score of 0.39, indicating its current strength may be unstable.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** US market breadth remains resilient with 45 of 144 groups in "all-green" territory, led by dominant tech hardware and industrial machinery, while precious metals and defense sectors experience sharp weekly declines.

The technology hardware and industrial machinery complexes continue to anchor market strength. Semiconductor Equipment & Materials, Electronic Components, and Farm & Heavy Construction Machinery remain entrenched as sustained momentum leaders. Meanwhile, a notable rotation is underway into consumer cyclicals and housing-related areas, with Airlines and Residential Construction both surging 28 spots in rank this week, signaling fresh interest in recovery plays.

Conversely, defensive havens and select heavy industries are rapidly losing ground. Aerospace & Defense plummeted 37 spots, while precious metals like Silver and Gold dropped 36 and 33 spots, respectively. We are also tracking early-stage divergences where high-momentum groups like Capital Markets and Semiconductors are starting to slip in rank, while low-momentum laggards like Beverages - Wineries & Distilleries are beginning to climb.

## Strength
* **Healthy Breadth:** A solid 45 of 144 industry groups maintain "all-green" status, showing positive performance across weekly, monthly, quarterly, half-year, and YTD horizons.
* **Dominant Leaders:** Semiconductor Equipment & Materials leads all groups with a momentum score of 0.977 (YTD rank 2), followed closely by Farm & Heavy Construction Machinery at 0.959 (YTD rank 6) and Electronic Components at 0.949 (YTD rank 5).
* **Sustained Performers:** Computer Hardware (momentum 0.930, YTD rank 1) and Electrical Equipment & Parts (momentum 0.876) continue to show robust, multi-month leadership.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Top Gainers:** Airlines (+28 spots to rank 47, momentum 0.84) and Residential Construction (+28 spots to rank 60, momentum 0.74) showed the strongest weekly rank improvements, alongside Diagnostics & Research (+19 spots to rank 107).
* **Top Losers:** Aerospace & Defense fell 37 spots to rank 73 (momentum 0.39), while Silver dropped 36 spots to rank 75 (momentum 0.33) and Gold lost 33 spots to land at rank 118 (momentum 0.21).
* **Momentum Laggards:** Bottom-tier momentum remains concentrated in Pharmaceutical Retailers (0.036 momentum, YTD rank 143), Broadcasting (0.071 momentum, YTD rank 138), and Financial Data & Stock Exchanges (0.075 momentum, YTD rank 134).

## Divergences
* **Fading Leaders:** High-momentum groups showing early rank declines include Capital Markets (momentum 0.61, rank -12 spots), Lodging (momentum 0.65, rank -9 spots), and Semiconductors (momentum 0.76, rank -4 spots).
* **Emerging Laggards:** Lower-momentum groups showing early rank improvements include Beverages - Wineries & Distilleries (rank +12, momentum 0.47) and Health Information Services (rank +11, momentum 0.48).
* **Defensive Rotation:** Both Auto & Truck Dealerships (momentum 0.41) and Utilities - Regulated Gas (momentum 0.47) jumped 10 spots in rank, signaling quiet accumulation in underperforming areas.
